questions.text:
Directions: The given sentence is divided into four parts A, B, C, and D. Choose the part that contains an error as your answer. If the sentence is error-free, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Running boosts cardiovascular health, improves mood, and increasing (A) overall stamina, making it an ideal exercise for individuals seeking (B) holistic wellness and improved fitness, it also serves as (C) a natural mood enhancer, triggering the release of endorphins. (D)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 1.

Key Points

  • Part A of the sentence i.e. 'running boosts cardiovascular health, improves mood, and increasing' is erroneous.
    • In the given sentence, the error lies in the inconsistency of verb forms. "Boosts" and "improves" are both verbs in the base form, but "increasing" is a gerund form. For proper parallelism, all of the three elements should be in the same grammatical form. 
    • To rectify this error, we need to replace "increasing" with its third-person present form which is "increases" to establish proper parallelism.
  • The correct sentence would be - Running boosts cardiovascular health, improves mood, and increases overall stamina, making it an ideal exercise for individuals seeking holistic wellness and improved fitness, it also serves as a natural mood enhancer, triggering the release of endorphins


Additional Information

  • Let's understand some important vocab given in the sentence - 
  • Cardiovascular - relating to the heart and blood vessels
    • For Example - 
    • Regular exercise, such as jogging, can improve cardiovascular health and strengthen the heart muscles.
  • Stamina - the ability to sustain prolonged physical or mental effort (सहनशीलता)
    • For Example - 
    • His daily jogging routine increased his stamina, allowing him to run longer distances without tiring.
  • Holistic - dealing with or treating the whole of something or someone and not just a part (संपूर्ण रूप से)
    • For Example - 
    • The holistic approach to wellness considers the interconnectedness of physical, mental, and emotional well-being.
  • Trigger - cause (an event or situation) to happen or exist (उत्प्रेरित)
    • For Example - 
    • The smell of freshly baked cookies can trigger feelings of warmth and nostalgia.

questions.text:
Directions: The given sentence is divided into four parts that are A, B, C, and D. Choose the part that contains an error as your answer. If the sentence is error-free, mark E i.e. 'No error' as your answer.

India will need to make concessions, knock (A) on doors, work the telephones and (B) burn the midnight oil if it wants to seek an (C) successful consensus at the conclusion of its Presidency. (D) No error (E)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 3.

Key Points

Part C of the sentence i.e. 'burn the midnight oil if it wants to seek an' is erroneous.

  • The use of article 'an' used before the adjective 'successful' is incorrect and it should be replaced with the article 'a' because the word 'successful' has a consonant sound to it.
  • Hence, the correct answer is C.
  • The correct sentence would be - India will need to make concessions, knock on doors, work the telephones and burn the midnight oil if it wants to seek a successful consensus at the conclusion of its Presidency.

​

Additional Information

​Let's understand the use of articles a, an, and the - 

  • Article 'a' is used before nouns that begin with a consonant sound.
    • For Example - 
    • I have a book in my purse.
  • (Here, article 'a' is used before the noun 'book' because it begins with a consonant sound)

 

  • Article 'an' is used before nouns that begin with a vowel sound.
    • For Example - 
    • Do you want an apple for breakfast?
  • (Here, the article 'an' is used before the noun 'apple' because it begins with a vowel sound)

 

  • Article 'the' is used before both singular and plural nouns when the noun is specific.
    • For Example - 
    • I saw the play you are talking about.
  • (Here, the article 'the' is used before the noun 'play' because it is the specific play that is being talked about)

questions.text:
Read the sentence below to find out if there is any error in it. The error, if any, will be in one part of the sentence. The letter of that part is the answer. If there is no error the answer is (5). (Ignore errors in punctuation if any).

We can not take any further risk at such (A)/crucial point because(B)/ market volatility is also increasing(C)/  with the increase in the number of cases. (D)/ No error(E)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 1.

 

  • In the given sentence error is in part A, The error is in the use of can not.
  • The thing to remember is when you use “not” with “can” to express a negative statement, you always put them together.
  • They actually become one word: “cannot”, and not “can not”.
  • This is the only time you join a modal verb with “not” into one.
  • But with the other models, “not” is always a separate word.

​Correct answer- We cannot take any further risk at such a crucial point market volatility is also increasing with the increase in the number of cases.

 

  • A modal verb is a type of verb that is used to indicate modality
    • Eg. likelihood, ability, permission, request, capacity, suggestions, order, obligation, or advice. ...
  • In English, the modal verbs commonly used are can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, and must..

questions.text:
Find the error in the given sentence. If there is no error mark 'None of the above.'

Kim offered only me twenty dollars to wash the whole house,(A) the amount being paid was very less.(B) It was less than the wages prescribed by (C) the Union in agreement with the government.(D)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 2) i.e. A.

Key Points

  • A modifier is a word, phrase, or clause that describes something or makes its meaning more specific. Modifiers function as adjectives or adverbs.
  • In part A, 'only' is the modifier for the phrase 'twenty dollars.'
    • Words like almost, even, exactly, hardly, just, merely, nearly, only, scarcely, and simply should come immediately before the word they modify.
    • Example: He was hardly late for the lecture.
    • Here, 'late' is the verb and it is being modified with the use of 'hardly'  
  • So in part A, the sentence should be: Kim offered me only twenty dollars to wash the whole house.
  • The use of the modifier 'only' should be such that it is placed before the noun phrase 'twenty dollars'.

Correct sentence: Kim offered me only twenty dollars to wash the whole house, the amount being paid was very less. It was less than the wages prescribed by the Union in agreement with the government.✔️

questions.text:
Read the sentence given below to find out if it contains any error. The error, if any, will be in one part of the sentence. If the sentence is error free, select No error or option 5. Ignore error of punctuation if any.

The massive melting of glaciers as (A)/ a result of global heating has (B)/ caused mark shifts in the Earth’s (C)/ axis of rotation since the 1990s.(D)/ No error (E)
questions.explanation:
The erroneous part is C i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

Key Points

  • The third part (C) of the sentence is erroneous the word 'mark' is not grammatically correct.
  • The word 'shifts' is a noun. Hence, an adjective should be used before the word to qualify the word.
  • So, the word 'mark' should be replaced with the adjective form, i.e. 'marked' which means 'noticeable'.
  • Hence, option 3) is the answer.


Correct sentence: The massive melting of glaciers as a result of global heating has caused marked shifts in the Earth’s axis of rotation since the 1990s.

Additional Information

  • An adjective is word which modifies a noun or a pronoun.
    • Example: She has bought a red scarf.

questions.text:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select “No improvement” option.

Russia’s candidate vaccine for COVID-19 appears to have been found a midwife in India.

options.text: appear to have been found a

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 4), i.e., appears to have found
Explanation 
  • It should be the perfect infinitive in the active voice instead of the perfect infinitive in the passive voice.
  • The perfect infinitive refers to a time before that of the preceding verb.
  • We form the perfect infinitive with to have + the past participle form of a verb.

​Additional Information

  • An infinitive = to + the base form of the verb. The infinitive functions as a noun, adjective, or adverb.
  • When infinitives are used without 'to', they are called bare infinitives.
  • We use the perfect infinitive after verbs such as claim, expect, hate, hope, like, love, prefer, pretend.
    • ​He pretended to have lost her number.
    • I'm glad to have studied at that school.

Correct sentence: Russia’s candidate vaccine for COVID-19 appears to have found a midwife in India.

questions.text:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select “No improvement” option.

The political and economic architecture of the emerging global order, which the allied powers shaped at the end of World War II, have been altered since then.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 4), i.e., has been altered since then
Explanation 
  • It should be the singular verb 'has' instead of the plural verb 'have'.
  • The subject 'the political and economic architecture' is singular, so it will take a singular verb according to the rules of the subject-verb agreement.
  • 'Political' and 'economic' are just adjectives. 'Architecture' is a noun, here, and hence the subject.

​Additional Information

  •  When the subject of a sentence is composed of two or more nouns or pronouns connected by and, use a plural verb.
    • Radha and Raveena are at the fair.
  • When a compound subject contains both a singular and a plural noun or pronoun joined by 'or' or 'nor', the verb should agree with the part of the subject that is closer to the verb.
    • Neither the actor nor the directors know where the actress has gone.
    • Neither the directors nor the actor knows where the actress has gone.
  • When there is a phrase or a clause that comes between the subject and the verb. The verb agrees with the subject, not with a noun or pronoun in the phrase.
    • One of the rooms is empty.
    • The task, which was given to me on Saturday, is difficult.
  • The words each, each one, either, neither, everyone, everybody, anybody, anyone, nobody, somebody, someone, and no one are singular and require a singular verb.
    • ​Each of the boys gets a prize.
    • Either of these roads leads to the railway station.
  • Emerging: become apparent or prominent.
  • Allied: joined by or relating to members of an alliance.
  • Altered: change in character or composition, typically in a comparatively small but significant way.

 

  • When two adjectives are joined by 'and' and qualify the same noun, then the subject, as a whole, is singular. 
    • A good and honest man are hard to find. 
    • A good and honest man is hard to find. 

​Correct sentence: The political and economic architecture of the emerging global order, which the allied powers shaped at the end of World War II, has been altered since then.

questions.text:
A sentence/a part of the sentence is underlined. Five alternatives are given to the underlined part which will improve the meaning of the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed, click the option corresponding to "No improvement". 

Food or otherwise, product development is usually a lengthy process that entails understanding consumer needs yet developing products accordingly.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is and developing.

Key Points

 The underlined phrase should be replaced because the conjunction 'yet' which means 'but nevertheless' is inappropriate for the sentence.

  • 'for' is a preposition so, it cannot be used to join the clauses. Hence, option 2) is not the answer.
  • 'but' is used to join the clauses which are contrasting with each other. 
    • Example: She will join us but we cannot wait for her.
    • The given clauses are not contrasting with each other. Therefore, option 4) should not be chosen.
  • 'and' should be chosen for the given sentence because the clauses should be written jointly.

Mistake Points

  • 'and' is used in option 1) and option 3).
  • The word 'products' is a noun and an adjective should be used with it to describe the word.
  • 'developing' is an adjective and 'develop' is a verb. Therefore, option 3) should be eliminated and option 1) should be chosen as the answer.


Correct sentence: Food or otherwise, product development is usually a lengthy process that entails understanding consumer needs and developing products accordingly.

Additional Information

A conjunction joins two words, phrases or sentences.

  • Example: Vijay is poor but he is honest.
                    Sam and Mark are joining us for lunch    .

questions.text:
A sentence/a part of the sentence is underlined. Five alternatives are given to the underlined part which will improve the meaning of the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed, click the option corresponding to "No improvement". 

IT services will remain a significant part of the job environment in India as the demand for talent and services continue to grow in the country.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is continues to.

Key Points

The underlined phrase should be replaced because the word 'continue' is incorrectly written.

  • The subject of the verb 'continue' is 'the demand' which is a singular noun.
  • Therefore, the word 'continues' should be used instead of 'continue'.
  • Hence, option 1) is the best fit.


Correct sentence: IT services will remain a significant part of the job environment in India as the demand for talent and services continues to grow in the country.

Additional Information

A verb shows an action or state of being.

  • Example: My mother is sleeping.
  • The subject and the verb should always agree in number. 
  • 'My mother' is a singular noun. That is why 'is' which is a singular verb is used here.

questions.text:
A sentence/a part of the sentence is underlined. Five alternatives are given to the underlined part which will improve the meaning of the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed, click the option corresponding to "No improvement". 

With the Covid-19 pandemic throwing up unique challenges, e-commerce majors were leaving no stone unturned in leveraging technology to woo customers.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is are leaving.

Key Points

The underlined phrase should be replaced because the word 'were' is not correct.

  • Past continuous tense is used to refer to a past event that was going on when another event took place.
    • Example: I was reading the newspaper when I heard the sound.
    • That is why the underlined phrase should be replaced.
    • Clearly, option 1) cannot be chosen.
  • Option 4) is inappropriate for this sentence. So, option 4) should be eliminated.
  • The sentence is hinting at an ongoing action. Hence, Present continuous tense can be used here. 

Mistake Points

  • Present continuous tense is used in both option 2) and option 3).
  • 'is' cannot be used because the subject of the verb i.e. 'e-commerce majors' is a plural noun. So, 'are' should be chosen.
  • Therefore, option 2) should be eliminated and option 3) should be chosen.


Correct sentence: With the Covid-19 pandemic throwing up unique challenges, e-commerce majors are leaving no stone unturned in leveraging technology to woo customers.

questions.text: According to the passage, what is one of the allegations Mr. Trump made against the World Health Organization (WHO)?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • Mr. Trump accused the World Health Organization (WHO) of being biased towards China.
  • This allegation was made in the context of the WHO's handling of the COVID-19 pandemic.
  • Mr. Trump reiterated this allegation by stating that the WHO was “owned and controlled by China.”
  • This accusation was one of the reasons for his decision to withdraw the United States from the WHO.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: “Mishandling of financial resources” – This was not mentioned as one of Mr. Trump’s allegations against the WHO in the passage.
  • Option 2: “Promoting fake medical news” – This was also not an allegation made by Mr. Trump in the passage.
  • Option 4: “Overestimating the COVID-19 impact” – Mr. Trump did not accuse the WHO of this in the passage.
  • Option 5: “Discriminating against African countries” – This was not part of the allegations mentioned in the passage.

questions.text: Which of the following has not been cited in the passage as a role of the WHO?

options.text: Implementing health programs for infectious diseases
Ensuring equity of access to life-saving drugs

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • The passage details several roles of the WHO, including implementing health programs for infectious diseases, ensuring equity of access to life-saving drugs, and detecting and preventing disease outbreaks.
  • The passage also highlights the importance of promoting collaboration among nations.
  • However, building stronger educational systems is not cited as a role of the WHO in the passage.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: “Implementing health programs for infectious diseases” – This is mentioned in the passage as one of the roles of the WHO.
  • Option 2: “Ensuring equity of access to life-saving drugs” – This is also mentioned in the passage as one of the roles of the WHO.
  • Option 4: “Detecting and preventing disease outbreaks” – This is mentioned in the passage as well.
  • Option 5: “Promoting collaboration among nations” – This is highlighted in the passage as an essential aspect of tackling pandemics.

questions.text: It can be inferred from the passage that the author's view on the U.S. withdrawal from WHO is:

options.text: Supportive, as it will lead to better management of funds
Neutral, as it will have no significant impact on global health
Oppositional, due to the potential negative impact on global health initiatives
Indifferent, because WHO will continue without U.S. contributions
Optimistic, that other countries will fill the funding gap left by the U.S.

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • The author describes Mr. Trump's decision to withdraw the U.S. from the WHO as "stunningly short sighted, and deeply concerning to the global health community."
  • The passage highlights the significant negative consequences of this decision, including the impact on health programs for HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, and other infectious diseases.
  • The author emphasizes the importance of collaboration among nations and the sharing of data and technology to address global health challenges.
  • These points indicate that the author is oppositional to the U.S. withdrawal from the WHO due to its potential negative impact on global health initiatives.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: “Supportive, as it will lead to better management of funds” – The author is clearly not supportive of the withdrawal.
  • Option 2: “Neutral, as it will have no significant impact on global health” – The author believes the withdrawal will have a significant negative impact on global health.
  • Option 4: “Indifferent, because WHO will continue without U.S. contributions” – The author is not indifferent but rather deeply concerned about the consequences of the withdrawal.
  • Option 5: “Optimistic, that other countries will fill the funding gap left by the U.S.” – The author does not express optimism that other countries will fill the funding gap.

questions.text: Which of the following best states the central idea of the passage?

options.text: The U.S. should prioritize its national interests over global organizations.
The U.S. withdrawal from WHO will have profound negative impacts on global health efforts.
WHO's funding structure needs reform to ensure fairness and equality.
Global collaboration is more important than ever in combating pandemics.
The U.S. health policies under President Trump have been highly beneficial.

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 2.
 
Key Points
  • The passage critiques the U.S. decision to withdraw from WHO, describing it as "stunningly short sighted" and highlights the potential negative impacts on global health initiatives.
  • The author details the crucial roles WHO plays in global health, including funding various health programs and ensuring equity of access to life-saving drugs.
  • The passage emphasizes the negative consequences of the U.S. withdrawal on these health efforts and the broader importance of global collaboration in combating pandemics.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: “The U.S. should prioritize its national interests over global organizations” – This is not the central idea of the passage. The author argues against the U.S. withdrawal from WHO.
  • Option 3: “WHO's funding structure needs reform to ensure fairness and equality” – The passage does not focus on the need for reforming WHO's funding structure.
  • Option 4: “Global collaboration is more important than ever in combating pandemics” – While the passage emphasizes the importance of global collaboration, the central idea is the negative impact of the U.S. withdrawal from WHO.
  • Option 5: “The U.S. health policies under President Trump have been highly beneficial” – The passage critiques President Trump's decision and does not argue that his health policies have been beneficial.

questions.text:
According to the passage, which of the following statements is correct?

A) WHO is a recent establishment with limited financial contributions from major countries.

B) Mr. Trump initiated a move to halt funding to WHO during his previous term as U.S. President.

C) The move to leave WHO requires a 12-month period before it is finalized.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 4.
 
Key Points
  • Statement A: WHO is a recent establishment with limited financial contributions from major countries.
    • This statement is incorrect as the passage mentions that WHO is a founding organization with significant contributions, especially from the U.S.
  • Statement B: Mr. Trump initiated a move to halt funding to WHO during his previous term as U.S. President.
    • This statement is correct as the passage confirms that Mr. Trump did initiate such a move during his previous term.
  • Statement C: The move to leave WHO requires a 12-month period before it is finalized.
    • This statement is correct as per the passage which mentions that the U.S. will leave WHO in 12 months and stop all financial contributions.
  • Hence, the correct statements are Statement B and Statement C.
Therefore, the correct answer is: ‘B and C’.

questions.text: What will fit in the blank taken from the passage: "As fantastic as it may sound, medicine is no _______ to miracles of science, and the health community hopes one more will restore the U.S. back to WHO’s fold."
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'stranger'.
 
Key Points
  • The word "stranger" fits the context of the sentence as it conveys that medicine is familiar with the miracles of science.
  • The phrase "medicine is no stranger to miracles of science" means that medical advancements frequently result from scientific breakthroughs.
  • Options 1, 2, 3, and 5 do not fit the context of the sentence correctly.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.
 
Complete Sentence: "As fantastic as it may sound, medicine is no stranger to miracles of science, and the health community hopes one more will restore the U.S. back to WHO’s fold."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "exception" is incorrect because it does not convey that medicine is familiar with miracles of science.
  • Option 2: "obstacle" is incorrect; "obstacle" indicates a hindrance, which is not suitable here.
  • Option 3: "gateway" is incorrect because it implies an entry point, which does not fit the context.
  • Option 5: "answer" is incorrect; the phrase would not make sense in the context.

questions.text: Which of the following words is similar in meaning to "petulance" in the context of the passage?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e., Irritability.

Key Points

  • The word "petulance" means being childishly sulky or bad-tempered. (चिड़चिड़ापन)
    • Example: His petulance was evident when he began to sulk after not getting his way.
  • "Irritability" refers to the quality of being easily annoyed or angered. (चिड़चिड़ापन)
    • Example: The teacher's irritability grew as the students continued to talk during the lecture.
  • Hence, we can infer that the word similar in meaning to 'petulance' is 'irritability'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Irritability.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Indifference (उदासीनता): Lack of interest, concern, or sympathy.
    • Example: His indifference to the suffering of others was quite startling.
  • Caution (सावधानी): Care taken to avoid danger or mistakes.
    • Example: He approached the wild animal with great caution.
  • Determination (दृढ़ संकल्प): Firmness of purpose; resoluteness.
    • Example: Her determination to succeed despite the odds was truly inspiring.
  • Wisdom (बुद्धिमत्ता): The quality of having experience, knowledge, and good judgement.
    • Example: With age comes wisdom, as they say.

questions.text: Which of the following words is opposite in meaning to "stunningly" in the context of the passage?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is: Option 3) i.e., Predictably.

Key Points

  • The word "stunningly" means something that causes astonishment or shock due to its unexpected nature. (चकित करने वाला)
    • Example: The magician's trick was so stunningly executed that everyone in the audience was left speechless.
  • "Predictably" refers to something that can be foreseen or anticipated beforehand. (पूर्वानुमानित)
    • Example: The outcome of the match was predictably in favour of the stronger team.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'stunningly' is 'predictably'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Predictably.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Surprisingly (हैरान करने वाला): Something that happens unexpectedly.
    • Example: Surprisingly, the underdog team won the championship.
  • Shocking (चौंकाने वाला): Something that causes intense surprise or disgust.
    • Example: The scandal was shocking to the entire community.
  • Amazingly (अद्भुत रूप से): In a way that causes great surprise or wonder.
    • Example: The athlete performed amazingly well at the Olympics.
  • Incredibly (अविश्वसनीय रूप से): Something that is hard to believe; extraordinary.
    • Example: The view from the mountain top was incredibly beautiful.

questions.text:
In the following question, two columns are given, containing three phrases each. A phrase from the first column may or may not connect with a phrase from the second column to make a grammatically and contextually correct sentence. There are five options, four of which display the sequence(s) in which the phrases can be joined to form a correct sentence. If none of the phrases make a correct sentence, mark ‘None of these’ as your answer.

Column (1)

Column (2)

(A) Schematic diagrams do not include details that are not 

(D) necessary for comprehending the information that the diagram was intended to convey.

(B) In a schematic diagram depicting an electrical circuit, one can see how the wires and components are

(E)  connected together, but not photographs of the circuit itself.

(C) Although schematic diagrams are 

(F) commonly associated with electrical circuits, many examples can be found in other industries.
questions.explanation:
Let's join the sentences to give a contextually and grammatically meaningful sentence. 

The correct sequences are:

A uses the negative 'not' already, so the next part should not contain any other word like 'but' that also expresses negation. It is only shown by D. So, A-D

B talks about 'wires and components', which 'are connected together' in E. So, B-E

B-D may seem to make a correct sentence; but it does not convey a full meaning, as opposed to B-E. Also, the reverse, A-E cannot form a coherent sentence., So, B-E is correct.

C uses the conjunction 'although', suggesting that the next part is a complete sentence (without any other conjunctions like 'but'), as given by F. So, C-F

Out of these, only B-E is expressed in the given options.

Therefore, the correct answer is option 3.

questions.text:
In the following question, two columns are given, containing three phrases each. A phrase from the first column may or may not connect with a phrase from the second column to make a grammatically and contextually correct sentence. There are five options, four of which display the sequence(s) in which the phrases can be joined to form a correct sentence. If none of the phrases make a correct sentence, mark ‘None of these’ as your answer.

Column (1)

Column (2)

(A) The CAG has found fault with Dassault Aviation being allowed to retain the gains made

(D) its absence in the 2016 contract is a clear benefit to the company. 

(B) Disappointingly, the CAG has not quantified the amount,

(E) by the absence of a bank guarantee, which, if executed, would have come with significant charges.

(C)The 2007 contract price offered by Dassault included bank charges, and

(F) though it declares that it should have been passed on to the Defence Ministry.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option (4) i.e. C-D and B-F

Key Points

Let's join the sentences to give a contextually and grammatically meaningful sentence. 

The correct sequences are:

  • A talks about 'gains' made, which is connected to the charges in E; and it also begins with 'by'. So, A-E
  • B gives a complete sentence; which suggests the next part must begin with a conjunction. This is given by 'though', which is F. So, B-F
  • C talks about 'contract price', which is related to '2016 contract' in D. So, C-D
  • Out of these, only C-D and B-F are expressed in the given options.
Therefore, the correct answer is option 4.
